model_reported.name: conduire-experience-optimisation
model_reported.summary: Proposed one measured follow-up that changes k-loop unrolling while retaining the selected parent’s parallel and SIMD strategy; preserved ordered accumulation, output clearing, arbitrary-size tail handling, and the thread cap.

model_reported.name: inspecter-environnement
model_reported.summary: This change uses the existing OpenMP constructs and no hardware-specific feature, so no additional environment inspection is needed to frame the experiment.

model_reported.name: consulter-documentation-technique
model_reported.summary: No new API, instruction, or uncertain compiler feature is introduced; the proposal uses the existing OpenMP SIMD and parallel-for constructs.

model_reported.name: evaluer-performances
model_reported.summary: Compared only the available three-sample historical means, distinguished row-parallel-only from row-parallel plus SIMD, and made no claim about the unmeasured proposal.

memory_lessons.applicability: The next bounded follow-up can test k unrolling while retaining the selected parent's row parallelism and SIMD; compare against both that parent and the faster row-parallel-only result.
memory_lessons.claim: The serial r-k-c variant measured 0.076396257 s, serial r-k-c with explicit SIMD measured 0.073052032 s, row-parallel r-k-c measured 0.009476691 s, and row-parallel plus SIMD measured 0.010415142 s. These results do not establish that SIMD helps when combined with row parallelism.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this unrolled variant on all official sizes, verify overwrite behavior and oracle tolerance, and compare repeated native n=1024 timings without attributing unmeasured gains.

proposal.hypothesis: Explicitly unrolling the k dimension by four in the selected row-parallel r-k-c SIMD kernel may reduce k-loop control overhead or expose useful scheduling to the compiler. The four contributions for each output element remain in ascending-k order, the tail handles arbitrary n, C is reset on every call, and worker count remains capped by min(threads,n). This tests unrolling as a follow-up; no performance gain is assumed.

retained: Within each output row, unroll the k traversal by four and apply four contributions in ascending-k order for each c; retain a scalar tail for all remaining k values.
Retain SIMD over contiguous c, static OpenMP parallelism over independent rows, and a worker cap of min(threads,n), with a serial path when the cap is at most one.
Continue clearing the complete output before accumulation to preserve overwrite behavior.
